summary: Proxy chunk boundary splits multibyte UTF-8 grapheme, causing truncated final character on SSE resumes
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that after an SSE connection resume (client reconnect + resume token) the final character of the streamed completion is sometimes replaced with a Unicode replacement character or missing entirely. Impact: end-user documents produced by LuminaDocs have truncated final punctuation or a corrupted emoji at the end of sentences in ~0.4% of resumed streams, causing downstream validation to fail. Environment: production, dedicated cluster in us-east, requests proxied through customer's on-prem nginx reverse proxy before reaching Redwood edge.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use LuminaDocs client with long-polling that drops connection and resumes using resume_id. 2) Start a streaming completion that ends with a multibyte grapheme (examples: emoji, accented character, or multi-codepoint emoji sequence). 3) Introduce a brief TCP interruption simulating client reconnect (e.g., kill socket or simulate flaky mobile network). 4) Observe resumed stream payload in browser or client: last grapheme appears as \uFFFD or is missing. Repro rate observed ~1/250 resumes for affected traffic patterns.
logs: Edge request id: req_0a1b2c3d; upstream response chunks show hex boundaries: ... 0xF0 0x9F 0x98 | 0x80 ... (split across two chunks). Nginx access log sample: 10.10.5.2 - - [10/Mar/2026:13:12:07 +0000] "GET /v1/stream?resume_id=abc123 HTTP/1.1" 200 0 "-" "User-Agent: LuminaClient/1.4"; Client-reported fragment: U+FFFD at end. Tcpdump snippet attached to customer thread (see Confluence).
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: customer's reverse proxy (nginx) is buffering and emitting chunked SSE frames which split multi-byte UTF-8 sequences at a buffer boundary, so the resume codec on client sees an incomplete code point and inserts replacement. Reproduced locally by configuring nginx with proxy_buffering on + small buffers. We validated by forcing chunk boundary at 1 byte increments; when chunk ends inside a multibyte UTF-8 codepoint the client receives replacement char. Redwood streaming encoder currently emits logical events but does not guarantee chunk boundaries align to UTF-8 codepoints when upstream (proxy) re-chunks the socket. Customer's nginx config: proxy_buffering on; proxy_buffers 4 8k; proxy_busy_buffers_size 8k.
comments: 2026-03-10 14:05 - Ava Chen: Customer reported via support form; attached example transcript and failing document. They said issue only after connection resume, not on initial stream.

2026-03-10 15:20 - Ravi Patel: Confirmed similar artifact in edge logs. Captured upstream chunk hex that splits 4-byte emoji across two writes. Filing as P1 given document validation failures for customer pipelines.

2026-03-11 09:10 - SRE Team: Reproduced locally by adding small proxy buffers; observed mismatch when nginx rewrites chunk boundaries. Created a minimal repro using curl + nginx conf and a test SSE server.

2026-03-11 11:35 - Eng (streaming-runtime): Ran a quick patch to ensure our SSE encoder flushes at UTF-8 boundary when emitting final event; created PR #2891 for review. Also advised customer to temporarily disable proxy_buffering or increase buffer size as workaround.
2026-03-12 08:40 - Customer (LuminaDocs): Applied temporary nginx change (proxy_buffering off) and reported a disappearance of the corrupted-character symptom in their quick smoke tests.
2026-03-12 12:00 - Ravi Patel: Scheduled staged rollout of runtime encoder patch to canary and will monitor resumed-stream error rate metric (stream.resume.utf8_errors).
2026-03-12 16:22 - Eng: Patch merged and release candidate built (v1.3.2-rc). Canaries show reduction from 0.4% -> 0.01% resumed-stream UTF8 errors.
resolution: Workaround: Customer to set 'proxy_buffering off' OR increase proxy_buffers / proxy_busy_buffers_size to avoid sub-byte chunking at proxy level; short-term change applied by LuminaDocs and confirmed mitigation. Permanent fix: streaming-runtime encoder change merged (PR #2891) to ensure flushes align to UTF-8 codepoint boundaries when emitting SSE events and when resume metadata is present. Rolled out v1.3.2-rc to canary on 2026-03-12 and scheduled gradual rollout to prod fleet pending monitoring over 48h. Follow-up: add an automated streaming test that simulates small-buffer proxies and assert no replacement characters on resume; add dashboard alert stream.resume.utf8_errors and docs entry in Streaming chunking guidelines.
